audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Level 3 to Vayne, but whys[2] and spikes[0] both call Level 3 Galio's 'one clean punish' and 'single best punish before her escape tools come fully online'. Two of the seven why-lines are also written for the wrong stage: whys[1] sits on the Level 2 row and discusses 'the level-1 trade', and whys[4] sits on the Level 6 row and discusses 'her first Kraken Slayer'.
audit.why: The one row where the page tells a Galio to fight is the row the chart tells him he loses, and the Level 6 row — the row where Hero's Entrance comes online and the entry's whole plan is 'roam' — is explained with an item spike. A reader scanning the chart and the matching line gets no usable signal at either point.
audit.corrected: Vayne, Vayne, Galio, Vayne, Skill, Vayne, Vayne, with whys[1] rewritten for Level 2 and whys[4] rewritten for Level 6.
sources: champ-data/galio.full.js (phases[4].side already 'Skill' with the Hero's Entrance line)
scratchpad packet galio.json entry vayne (38.98%, 59 games)

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers are built on 'trade on the Condemn cooldown' — breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0], report[5], tldr, winCon — and never once state what that cooldown is. Tumble and Final Hour are likewise unnumbered.
audit.why: Condemn is 20/18/16/14/12. Twenty seconds at rank 1 is an enormous window in a lane the entry otherwise describes as unwinnable, and it is the single most useful number on the page. Tumble is 6/5/4/3/2 — by rank 5 a two-second reset she can hold through your whole combo — and Final Hour is 100/85/70.
audit.corrected: Condemn 20s at rank 1 falling to 12s; Tumble 6s falling to 2s; Final Hour 100s at rank 1. The 20 seconds after a spent Condemn is your only all-in window in the entire lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[0] and early both say Vayne out-ranges Galio — 'she pokes you off the wave with Tumble-autos and range from turn one', 'farm with Q windblasts from max range' — with no numbers.
audit.why: Vayne's attack range and Condemn are both 550. Winds of War is 825. Galio out-ranges Vayne by 275 units with his only poke tool, which inverts the framing: he does not have to concede the poke war, he has to refuse the auto war. This is the most actionable correction available in the matchup and it is absent from both layers.
audit.corrected: Winds of War reaches 825 against her 550 attack range and 550 Condemn. You out-range her — poke from 825 and never contest inside 550.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vayne.json (E Condemn range 550; Vayne's basic attack range 550)

audit.whatIsWrong: Condemn is described five times as a 'wall-stun' with no mention that the stun is conditional on terrain.
audit.why: Condemn knocks the target back and only impales and stuns them if they collide with terrain. Fought in the open lane it is a knockback and nothing more. That turns a passive fear ('she Condemns you into a wall') into a positioning rule ('keep the wall off your back'), which is the only lever a Galio actually has against it.
audit.corrected: Condemn only stuns if the knockback puts you into terrain — fight with open ground behind you and it is a reposition, not a stun.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vayne.json (E Condemn: 'knocking them back... If they collide with terrain, they are impaled, dealing bonus damage and stunning them', flags projectile,knockup,hardCC,terrain)

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[2].why says 'the dash is interruptible and root-able mid-flight'.
audit.why: Justice Punch cannot be interrupted once it is travelling, and Vayne has no root at all — Condemn is a knockback, Tumble is a self-dash, Final Hour is a self-buff. The line invents an answer she does not own instead of naming the one she does.
audit.corrected: Vayne has no root. Justice Punch cannot be interrupted mid-travel; what beats it is the 550-range Condemn fired before you commit, which is why the punch goes out on its cooldown.
sources: wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Galio (Justice Punch cannot be interrupted mid-travel)

audit.whatIsWrong: Tumble is never identified as an auto-attack reset, and Silver Bolts is described as procing off attacks only.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags 'autoreset-burst-tell: Vayne's combo opens with an auto-attack reset (Tumble (Q))', and the kit confirms the autoReset flag. Silver Bolts procs on 'the third consecutive attack or ability against the same target' — so the third stack can arrive faster than three visible autos suggest. Together they mean her burst window is shorter than the entry implies, and the Tumble wind-up is the release cue for the taunt.
audit.corrected: Tumble is an auto-reset, so her opener is auto into instant empowered auto. Silver Bolts stacks on attacks or abilities, so the true-damage third hit lands sooner than three autos.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vayne.json (Q Tumble flags: autoReset; W Silver Bolts: 'third consecutive attack or ability against the same target')

audit.why: The entry's central claim — Silver Bolts is percent-max-health TRUE damage, so neither armour nor Shield of Durand touches it — is correct and well stated in early, whys[4..6] and wants.foe[1]. The kit confirms the trueDamage flag. I left that argument alone and only attached the shield's real number where it was vague.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer refers to Vayne as 'he' and 'his' throughout the lines it shares with every other matchup: dontsFull[0] 'E-punch into his Condemn', dontsFull[0].d 'half his win condition', dontsFull[2].d and tradeBad 'Justice Punching into his full kit'.
audit.why: These are template strings that were never gendered per champion. It is a small thing on one line and a credibility problem when it appears four times on a page about Vayne.
audit.corrected: Use 'her' in the Vayne-specific lines. I have fixed the ones I am already editing; tradeBad, breakdown.trading and report[3].t carry the same 'his full kit' phrasing and are noted for the applier.

audit.why: 38.98% over 59 games with HARD, 7.5/10 difficulty and a 9.5/10 carry threat. Those labels already match the data, unlike the Urgot entry.

edits.after: - Vayne Condemn: matchup-defining — 20s at rank 1, and it only stuns if a wall is behind you. That downtime is your window. - Her Tumble: 6s at rank 1, down to 2s, and it resets her auto. - Your R: spend it on allies' fights.

edits.before: That is Vayne's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.

edits.after: You have one ability and no engage at Level 1, but you out-range her 825 to 550 — chip with Winds of War and refuse the auto war.

edits.after: Level 2 is hers: Tumble is a 6-second auto-reset, so she steps in from 550, lands an empowered auto and leaves before your taunt can finish charging.

edits.after: Hold Condemn for your commit and aim it at a wall — without terrain behind you it only shoves, with terrain it stuns

edits.before: Q-W-E online: if she steps into Tumble-auto range to last-hit, channel Shield of Durand for the taunt and Justice Punch the knockup through her — your one clean punish before Final Hour gives her stealth to escape.
edits.after: Q-W-E online: your punish is a spent Condemn, not a step-up. It is 20 seconds at rank 1, so the moment she fires it, channel Shield of Durand for the taunt and Justice Punch the knockup through her before Final Hour exists.

edits.before: Vayne's Tumble + range mean she walks backward out of your Justice Punch every time, and Shield of Durand does almost nothing to her because Silver Bolts are TRUE damage — your whole anti-magic identity is wasted in this lane. At Level 1 you have only Winds of War and no engage, so concede the opening and farm with Q windblasts from max range. Your only early bait: if she over-extends to last-hit in your face, you can channel W for the taunt and E the knockup through her — but a good Vayne won't give you that step-in.
edits.after: Vayne's Tumble + range mean she walks backward out of your Justice Punch every time, and Shield of Durand does almost nothing because Silver Bolts is TRUE damage — your whole anti-magic identity is wasted here. But you do out-range her: Winds of War is 825 against a 550 attack range, so concede the auto war and chip her off the wave from outside it. Your one early bait is a spent Condemn — it runs 20 seconds at rank 1, and it only stuns if terrain is behind you, so hold your ground in open lane and punch in once she has fired it.

edits.before: Level 3 with Q-W-E up is your one respectable trading window — punish any step-up with Shield of Durand's taunt into a Justice Punch knockup before Final Hour gives her Tumble stealth to break it. But she only needs to land one Condemn to knock you into a wall and reset the trade in her favor. At 6, stop forcing the 1v1: Hero's Entrance is global, so flag a fight in another lane and drop the landing taunt to swing the map — that roam, not the duel, is where your value lives.
edits.after: Level 3 is your one respectable window, and it opens on a spent Condemn rather than on her step-up — 20 seconds at rank 1 is long enough to taunt and Justice Punch through her before Final Hour gives Tumble stealth. Keep open ground behind you: the knockback only stuns on terrain collision. At 6, stop forcing the 1v1 — Hero's Entrance is global, so flag a fight in another lane and drop the landing taunt. That roam, not the duel, is where your value lives.

Galio facts verified at wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Galio and reused across this slice: Shield of Durand cuts magic 25/30/35/40/45% and physical exactly half (12.5/15/17.5/20/22.5%), passive magic shield 7.5/9/10.5/12/13.5% max health restoring after 12/10/8s out of combat, taunt on release with radius 175-350 and 0.5-1.5s by channel time. Justice Punch knocks up 0.75s, cannot be interrupted mid-travel, is disabled while Grounded, halts on terrain or champions. Winds of War 825, tornado 2s, no slow. Hero's Entrance channels 2.75s, CC-immune after 1.25s. Colossal Smash is a 5s empowered auto scaling with 60% bonus MR.
